co_trojan_bunny_buttress.blurb: A broad, complicated granite buttress on the south wall of the South Fork of St. Vrain Canyon, a short drive from Lyons. The 23 routes split between sport lines and gear climbs, mostly one pitch with a few that go to two. Difficulty skews hard: one easy-ish entry around 5.8 and a couple of 5.9s, then a thick middle band in the 5.11s and 5.12s and a few at 5.13 or above, so it suits stronger leaders more than beginners. The rock offers roofs, edges, flakes and cracks, and the main faces look north, with a few west and east walls. Older bolted slabs can want some cams.

co_black_widow_slab.blurb: A lower-angled granite slab in the narrows of Boulder Canyon, on the south side of the highway just upstream of the much steeper Vampire Rock. Visitors find a mix of bolted face climbs and gear routes, about 23 in all, running from the 5.8 range up through a thick block of 5.10s and 5.11s, with a few 5.12s and one harder line. Several of the bolted lines are around 100 feet and want a long rope for lowering. A fern-filled gully separates this slab from its taller neighbour. In cold winters the same walls grow ice and mixed lines, which is what the place is best known for.

co_castle_the_climbs.blurb: A big pink-granite crag on the northern fringe of the South Platte, near Wellington Lake southwest of Bailey. The 23 routes here are all gear-protected, many following cracks, and some run as long as six pitches. Nearly all of them fall in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, with the largest group at 5.10, plus one far easier line. Walls look both north and south, with clean rock that carries some of the knobby features seen at Devil's Head. It is a long hike from the lake and a place for people comfortable placing their own protection and managing multi-pitch descents. Warm months are the usual time to go.

co_left_field.blurb: A small quartzite sport crag just south of Ouray along the Million Dollar Highway, at roughly 9,500 feet. Most of its 23 routes are bolted, with a couple of gear lines and a few top-rope options, on very hard, fine-grained rock. Grades run from an easy 5.3 up to the low 5.12s and 5.13, though the bulk sit between 5.9 and 5.11, which makes it a decent pick for climbers working through the 5.10s. The cliff looks northeast, picking up early light before going into shade for the rest of the day, so it is a comfortable choice when the weather is warm. Expect about a quarter hour of uphill walking.

co_emerald_isle_the.blurb: The largest of the cliffs at Heaven's Gate, a quiet sport-climbing zone south of Elevenmile Canyon in the South Platte. Nearly all of the 23 routes are bolted, with just one gear line, on granite that includes an overhanging alcove. The spread is wide: a few climbs in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, a solid group of 5.10s and 5.11s, and a decent number of 5.12s and 5.13s with one harder line on top. The wall faces southwest and offers more variety than its two neighbours. Getting to the base means a short uphill walk and a little scrambling.

co_turret_dome.blurb: The biggest rock in Elevenmile Canyon, a granite dome near Lake George about four miles up the canyon road. The south face carries multi-pitch routes with occasional run-out stretches, while the west face is shorter and steeper. Of the 23 routes, about half use natural protection and half are bolted. It is a good place for newer climbers, since many lines sit between easy scrambling and 5.7, with a big chunk at 5.9 and 5.10 and one harder 5.12. Clean, grippy granite and lots of sun keep the rock dry; spring and fall are comfortable seasons, and midday can get hot.

co_valhalla_2.blurb: A far-flung wall at the top end of Thunder Ridge in the West Creek area of the South Platte, sitting well above and beyond the main ridge crags. The 23 routes are mostly gear-protected or mixed, where bolts need supplementing, on faceted granite with chickenheads and patina. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Middle routes reach about 115 feet, so a 70 meter rope helps. The face points southwest and takes plenty of sun, which makes it a pleasant choice on mild days. The hike is long, roughly two and a half miles, and wind can funnel through the valley.

_skipped.co_engineering_center: Concrete building walls on the CU campus (buildering) that the page flags as illegal; not a climbing crag.
